title: Dimension functions restrict to strict localizations and are tested there
statement: Let $T$ be a Noetherian excellent scheme [def-exc-excellent-ring]. For a geometric point $\bar t$ above $t\in T$, let $\pi_{\bar t}:T_{(\bar t)}\to T$ be its strict localization [def-weil-geometric-point, def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]. A dimension function on a scheme $S$ means a function $d:|S|\to\mathbf Z$ whose value decreases by one at every immediate geometric specialization: the reduced closure of the general point in the strict localization at the special geometric point has Krull dimension one [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. For every function $d:|T|\to\mathbf Z$, the function $d$ is a dimension function if and only if $d\circ|\pi_{\bar t}|$ is a dimension function on $T_{(\bar t)}$ for every geometric point $\bar t$ of $T$. In particular every dimension function on $T$ pulls back to a dimension function on each strict localization.

source.place: Expose XIV, Definition 2.1.8 and the following paragraph (etale restriction and locality), printed pp.211–212; strict-local version used at the start of the proof of Proposition 2.5.4, printed p.217.
